This adjustment increased their pressing intensity (press from 0.66 to 0.84), line height (0.6 to 0.72), and directness of play (0.42 to 0.57).
- The style change aimed to exploit wider spaces and quickly transition the ball forward, reflecting their usual wide, crossing approach but with greater urgency and risk by pressing higher and delivering more direct balls.
- Following the change, Seabrook's possession remained stable (around 54%), but field tilt dropped from 70% to 48%, and their expected goals (xG) decreased from 0.78 to 0.46, suggesting the more direct, high-press approach led to fewer quality chances and reduced territorial dominance against Harbour City’s disciplined 4-2-3-1 patient short passing style.
- Harbour City absorbed the increased pressure effectively, as reflected by their low opponent xG rising only slightly (0.03 to 0.14), showing resilience to the pressing trap while maintaining overall defensive stability.
